summary: AuthN is proving who you are (X-API-Key -> 401 without/wrong key). AuthZ is what that principal may see (principal-b GET of A's link is 404, not 200 with A's URL). Redirect stays public so humans and crawlers can follow short links without a key.
evidence: Authentication: NO_AUTH_CREATE_STATUS 401 API key required; BAD_KEY_CREATE_STATUS 401 Invalid API key; CREATE_A_STATUS 200 with X-API-Key A. Authorization: GET_A_AS_A 200; GET_A_AS_B 404 Link not found (no long_url leak); DELETE_A_AS_B 404; A_STILL_OWNS 200.

Revoke on leak: keys live in API_KEYS map; remove/rotate the leaked value (or JWT_SECRET if that alias was used) and the next request is 401 Invalid API key. No expiry on API keys — revoke is rotation, which is why we chose API key over JWT for this internal admin surface.

Redirect remains public: GET /r/55c6dbbb with no X-API-Key returned 307 Location https://example.com/a. Short links are the product; requiring a key would break every shared URL. Abuse is handled by redirect_per_min=8 (429 after 8 hits), not by hiding the redirect behind auth.
